description: A geospatial dataset and interactive map of potential pumped storage hydropower (PSH) sites in the United States, characterising the quantity, quality and cost of the resource. Contents: fields on storage duration, paired reservoir volume, capacity, distance between reservoirs, head height, transmission spur line distance and cost, and total cost. Sites are closed-loop, or use existing reservoirs along rivers, repurpose open-pit mines, or pair dry-gully reservoirs with ring dams. The method adapts the Australian National University global greenfield pumped hydro atlas: 30 m elevation models, head height 200 to 750 m, dam heights of 40 to 100 m for dry gullies and 15 to 25 m for ring dams, upper and lower reservoir capacity within 10%, exclusions for water bodies, glaciers, protected federal lands, urban areas and critical habitat, and existing reservoirs from HydroLAKES. Producer: NLR geospatial science group. Coverage: United States. Format and access: download from the interactive map at maps.nlr.gov/psh. Free. Licence: not stated on the page read. Caveats: technical potential from geometry and screening, not permitted projects. Simulation uses: storage siting and cost inputs to capacity expansion models such as ReEDS. Related records: the Open Energy Data Initiative record and the NLR Siting Lab record.
